After the downfall of the Delhi Sultanate, who was the first ruler to issue the gold coin?

s: Arrange properly as per dates of four important battles fought by Humayun, the names of battlefields are given below –
x: The correct order of battles fought by Humayun is as follows- Devara (Daurah), Chausa, Kannauj and Sirhind. Humayun defeated Afghan rebels on the banks of Gomati at Devara or Daurah in 1532 A.D. Sher Shah defeated Humayun in the Battle of Chausa on 26 June 1539 AD in which a water fetcher named Nizam saved his life. This victory against Humayun increased the prestige and power of Sher Shah. He read ‘Khutba’ by his name, occupying the title of Sher Shah and engraved this on the coins. On 17th May, 1540 AD Humayun was again defeated by Sher Shah in the Battle of Kanauj (Bilgram) and Humayun fled from one place to the other after this war. Humayun occupied Delhi after the Battle of Sirhind on 22th June, 1555 AD.

s: According to ‘Rao-Jaitsi-Ro-Chhanda’, who among the following was defeated by Rao Jaitsi, the ruler of Bikaner?
x: After the death of Mughal Emperor Babur, his son Humayun ascended the Mughal throne. After coming to power, Humayun wanted to establish firm control over northern India by subduing the Rajput states. To achieve this, he sent his brother Kamran Mirza against Rao Jaitsi (or Rao Jait Singh), the independent ruler of Bikaner, in the 1530s. According to Beethu Souza’s text Rao-Jaitsi-Ro-Chhanda, a battle took place between Kamran and Rao Jaitsi, in which Rao Jaitsi defeated Kamran. 4. Who among the following made an offer to Humayun that he would surrender Bihar and pay an annual tribute of 10 lakh dinars if he was allowed to retain Bengal? Which of the following two rulers fought the battle near Kannauj of 17th May 1540? (a) Humayun and Sultan Mohammad Nuhani (b) Shershah and Humayun (c) Shershah and Mirza Kamran (d) Mohammad Shah and Humayun U.P.B.E.O. (Pre) 2019 Ans. (b) Shershah Suri & Humayun fought the battle near Kannauj on 17th May 1540 AD. Shershah defeated Humayun. Since the battle was fought in an ancient town, Bilgram (now municipal board in Hardoi district, U.P.), it is also called Battle of Bilgram.

s: When Humayun invaded Chunar Fort first time?
x: Humayun invaded Chunar Fort for the first time in 1532 AD. Humayun besieged this fort for four months, and after that, Sher Khan accepted his supremacy. In addition to this, he invaded Kalinjar in 1531 AD and annexed Raisina fort in 1535 AD.

s: When did Humayun first attacked Chunar Fort?
x: Humayun besieged Chunar Fort in 1532 for four months, after which Sher Khan accepted his supremacy. The 1531 date belongs to the Kalinjar invasion, so option 1 is wrong.

s: Between whom was the Battle of Chausa fought?
o: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat and Humayun

s: From the following names identify the one who was not the brother of Humayun.

x: The Safavid Shah Tahmasp of Persia helped him retake Kandahar and Kabul.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

s: In which fort was the Sher Mandal library, from whose stairs Humayun fell to his death in January 1556?
x: He fell from the stairs of the Sher Mandal library in the Purana Qila, Delhi.

s: Who is the author of the Humayun-nama?
x: The Humayun-nama was written by Humayun's sister Gulbadan Begum. Hamida Banu Begum was Humayun's wife and Akbar's mother; Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama; Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi.

x: Kannauj is also called the Battle of Bilgram.

x: After Panipat Babur occupied Delhi and Agra.

o: It was fought in 1539 between Babur and Mahmud Lodi.

s: From which place were Jayata and Kumpa associated who impressed Shershah with their valour?

x: Sher Khan assumed the title of ‘Hazrat-e-Ala’ after defeating the ruler of Bengal, Nusrat Shah. Which improvements among these were done by Sher Shah Suri? (1) Revenue reforms (2) Administrative reforms (3) Military reforms (4) Currency system reforms Select the right answer by using code given below – (a) 1 and 2 (b) 1,2 and 3 (c) 2,3 and 4 (d) all the above Uttarakhand P.C.S. s: Where is Mausoleum of Sher Shah ?
x: The tomb of Sher Shah is an imposing brick structure partly veneered with stone standing in the middle of a tank. This tomb is located at Sasaram of Rohtas in Bihar. It is regarded as one of the noblest specimens of Afghan architecture in India.

s: Sher Shah was buried at –

s:

II. He administered Sarkar and Paragana directly without using any other officials.

Consider the following statements on Sher Shah's land revenue administration:
I. Land was classified into three categories on the basis of produce from the land.
II. Land was measured according to a uniform system.
III. 1/4 of the produce was collected as tax.
Which of the above statements are correct?
x: Sher Shah Suri reformed the Mughal revenue system. Land was measured systematically and categorized based on productivity. However, the tax was generally one-third of the produce, not one-fourth. Therefore statements I and II are correct.

s: Which medieval ruler introduced the system of “patta” and “qabuliyat” to help the peasants?
x: Sher Shah was a medieval ruler who introduced the system of ‘’patta’’ and ‘’qabuliyat’’ to help the peasants.The peasants were given ‘’patta’’ by the central authority, in which the share of the government was clearly mentioned. The peasants accepted it through ‘’qabuliyat’’.

s: Kabuliyat and Patta was introduced by
x: Patta (title deed) and qabuliyat (deed of acceptance) were introduced by Sher Shah as part of his land revenue settlement, not by Shivaji, Jahangir or Aurangzeb.

s: Kabuliyat and Patta as instruments of settlement were introduced by
x: Sher Shah introduced the patta and qabuliyat as instruments of direct state-peasant settlement; the other rulers listed did not.

s: The rate of land tax levied by Shershah was
x: Sher Shah Suri levied a land tax at the rate of one-third of the produce under his revenue administration, based on careful measurement and assessment.

s: Which measure did Sher Shah's land survey use to measure land uniformly?
x: Land was measured with the sikandari gaz and the jarib, and classified into good, middling and bad.

s: In Sher Shah's revenue system, what was the Qabuliyat?
o: the title deed given to the peasant stating his revenue dues
the deed of agreement signed by the peasant accepting the revenue demand
the fee paid to the surveyor
the fee paid to the revenue collector
x: The Qabuliyat was the peasant's deed of acceptance of the revenue demand, signed by him. The Patta was the title deed given to the cultivator. Jaribana was the surveyor's fee and muhasilana the collector's fee.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the revenue systems of Sher Shah and Akbar-Todar Mal?
o: Sher Shah classified land into three categories.
Akbar-Todar Mal used four land classes: polaj, parauti, chachar and banjar.
Akbar-Todar Mal retained the one-third share but used ten-year averages.
Sher Shah fixed the state's share at one-fourth of average produce.
x: Sher Shah's rate was one-third of average produce, not one-fourth; the other three statements are correct.

s: Under Sher Shah, to whom was the 'jaribana' fee paid?
x: Jaribana was the surveyor's fee; muhasilana was the collector's fee.

s: What was the state's share of land revenue under Sher Shah?
x: The state share was one-third of average produce; the system became the model for Todar Mal's Bandobast.

s: Under Sher Shah, what was the 'muhasilana'?
o: The fee paid to the revenue collector
The fee paid to the surveyor
The title deed given to the cultivator
The deed of acceptance signed by the peasant
x: Muhasilana was the collector's fee; jaribana was the surveyor's fee.

s: Who introduced coin of silver?
x: Sher Shah is honoured for the establishment of the reformed currency system, which circulated during the Mughal period and became the basis of British currency. He introduced pure gold, silver and copper coins as well as abolished currency coins of mixed metal, which had fixed-rate and sizes. His silver rupee coins weighed 178 grains of which 173 grains were pure silver. Sher Shah’s name, title and place of mint were invariably inscribed on the coins in Arabic language and Devanagari script.

s: What was the exchange rate of silver’s rupiya ?

s: Hem Chandra Vikramaditya is famous in Indian history as –
x: Hemu was also known as Hem Chandra Vikramaditya. Hemu rose to become chief of the army and Prime Minister to Adil Shah Suri of the Sur dynasty. Hemu won the Battle against Targi Begh and assumed the title of Vikramaditya that had been earlier adopted by many Hindu kings since Vedic times. x: The Mughal army had the largest number of Hindu Generals during the reign of Aurangzeb. There were 31.6% Hindu commanders in Aurangzeb’s court in which most of the members were Marathas. This ratio was 22.5% in Akbar’s reign and 22.4% during Shah Jahan’s reign.

s: Which Mughal Emperor was known as "Zinda Peer" ?
x: Aurangzeb was a remarkable man. Among the Mughals, he possessed extraordinary personal qualities. He maintained high moral standards and was far from vices, pleasures and extravagance. Some recommended him ‘Shahi Darvesh’ and some Muslims accepted him as "Zinda Peer".

s: Which of the following Mughal Emperors wrote his autobiography in Persian ?
x: Jahangir was an outstanding author as well as a critic. He wrote his autobiography in Persian language and named it Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri. Jahangir had recorded his merits as well as demerits in his autobiography. This memoir has been divided into three parts. The first part is the preface which was written by Muhammad Hadi after the death of Jahangir in which the early life of Jahangir is mentioned. The second part was an original piece of text narrated by Jahangir. The third part of the text was written by Muhammad Hadi. Babur wrote his autobiography ‘Tuzuk-i-Babri’’ in the Turkish language.

s: Which of the following is an incorrect sequence of Mughal rulers?
x: The Mughal order is Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb. Akbar, Shah Jahan, Jahangir reverses the last two, so it is the incorrect sequence.

s: The Mughal Emperor who prohibited the use of tobacco was
x: Jahangir banned tobacco smoking in his reign. The notes do not state this, but Akbar, Babur and Aurangzeb are not known for the ban.

s: Which Mughal ruler of the following has learnt Hindu music from Lala Kalavant?
x: Akbar, a great patron of music, learnt Hindu music from Lala Kalavant. The notes do not mention this fact.

s: The Sufi saint of Naqshbandiya order, Ubaidullah Ahrar was followed by which among the following Mughal Emperor?
x: The notes say the Naqshbandi order came to India with Babur, so Babur is the Mughal emperor who followed the Naqshbandi saint Ubaidullah Ahrar. Akbar's Sulh-i-Kul was opposed by the Naqshbandis.

s: Who of the following Mughal Emperor was coronated twice?
Which Mughal Emperor Started Hijri Samvat in India by replacing Illahi samvat?
Which Mughal Emperor wrote his own autobiography?
Which of the following statements about the Mughal emperors is correct?
o: Babur adopted the title Zinda Pir.
Shah Jahan received the title 'Shah Jahan' from Jahangir.
Aurangzeb was known as Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir.
x: Jahangir gave Prince Khurram the title 'Shah Jahan'. Alamgir and Zinda Pir were associated with Aurangzeb, while Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir was Jahangir's title.

s: Which of the following describes Jahangir's religious policy?
o: A complete break from Akbar's tolerance
Broadly continuing Akbar's tolerance, though Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons
x: Jahangir broadly continued Akbar's tolerance; Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons linked to support for the rebel prince Khusrau.

s: Under which emperor did the Mughal Empire reach its maximum territorial extent?
x: Aurangzeb's Deccan conquests of Bijapur and Golconda gave the empire its greatest extent.

s: Which Mughal emperor, slightly more orthodox than Akbar, destroyed some newly built temples yet kept many Hindu nobles?
x: Shah Jahan was slightly more orthodox and destroyed some newly built temples but continued to employ many Hindu nobles.

s: In which year did Aurangzeb reimpose jizya?
x: Aurangzeb reimposed jizya in 1679 and banned festivals such as Navroz.

s: Which traditions does Dara Shikoh's Majma-ul-Bahrain bring together?
x: Majma-ul-Bahrain ('mingling of two oceans') compares Sufism and Vedanta.

s: Of which text is Dara Shikoh's Sirr-i-Akbar (1657) a Persian translation?
x: Sirr-i-Akbar is the Persian Upanishads (1657); the Mahabharata became the Razmnama under Akbar.

s: In which language was Babur's memoir, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi, written?
x: Babur wrote in Turki; Jahangir's Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri was in Persian.

s: Which Mughal emperor was unlettered but introduced educational reforms covering arithmetic, logic, astronomy and agriculture?
x: Akbar could not read or write, yet he was a great patron of learning and widened the curriculum.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Humayun was learned in Persian, Arabic and Turkish.
2. Jahangir wrote his memoirs, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, in Persian.
3. Akbar wrote an autobiography in Turki.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Humayun was learned and Jahangir wrote in Persian; Akbar was unlettered and wrote no autobiography.

s: In which language did Jahangir write his memoirs, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri?
x: Jahangir wrote the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri in Persian, unlike Babur, who wrote in Turki.

s: Under which Mughal emperor was the share of Hindu nobles in the nobility the highest?
x: Hindu nobles formed about 31.6% under Aurangzeb, against about 22.5% under Akbar.

s:
Consider the following statements about Hindu nobles in Mughal service:
1. Their share under Aurangzeb was higher than under Akbar.
2. Most Hindu nobles added under Aurangzeb were Marathas from the Deccan wars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Under Aurangzeb Hindu nobles rose to about 31.6%, mostly Marathas taken in during the Deccan wars.

s: Which Mughal emperor banned the celebration of Navroz?
x: Aurangzeb, who also reimposed jizya in 1679, banned Navroz.

s: Who was the Mughal Emperor, who issued farman to East India Company to start a factory at Surat?
Which work was written by Guru Gobind Singh, who fought 14 wars against Aurangzeb's forces?
x: Guru Gobind Singh wrote the Zafarnama, which advocated the sword only when all other avenues failed.

s: The Chali Mukte are associated with which event?
o: The release of Guru Hargobind from Gwalior Fort
The founding of the Khalsa at Anandpur
The compilation of the Adi Granth at Amritsar
The defence of Guru Gobind Singh at Muktsar
x: The Chali Mukte, or 40 liberated ones, died defending Guru Gobind Singh at Muktsar; the event is commemorated as Maghi.

s: In which year did Guru Gobind Singh found the Khalsa on Baisakhi day?
x: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa on 13 April 1699 (Baisakhi) with the Panj Pyaras. 1675 is Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom, and 1710 is Banda Singh Bahadur's conquest of Sirhind; 1704 is not the Khalsa's date.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sis Ganj — Cremation place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Rakab Ganj — Execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Sis Ganj — Execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Muktsar — Execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur
x: Sis Ganj marks the execution place of Guru Tegh Bahadur, while Rakab Ganj marks his cremation place.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Baisakhi — Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind
Baisakhi — foundation day of the Khalsa
Shaheedi Divas — martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur
Sirhind Fateh Diwas — Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind
x: Baisakhi is associated with the foundation of the Khalsa, not Banda Singh Bahadur’s conquest of Sirhind. The conquest is commemorated by Sirhind Fateh Diwas.

s: Who compiled the Adi Granth in 1604?
x: Guru Arjan compiled the Adi Granth in 1604.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Guru Hargobind — compilation of Adi Granth
x: Guru Hargobind built the Akal Takht, was imprisoned at Gwalior and fought at Kartarpur. The Adi Granth was compiled by Guru Arjan Dev.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Guru Tegh Bahadur?
o: He was the ninth Sikh Guru, born Tyag Mal in 1621.
He was executed by Jahangir in 1606.
x: Execution by Jahangir in 1606 describes Guru Arjan Dev; Tegh Bahadur was executed on Aurangzeb's orders in Delhi in 1675.

s: Which was the capital of Banda Singh Bahadur's Sikh state?
x: Banda Singh Bahadur's capital was Lohgarh; Anandpur Sahib was founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur.

s: How was Bhakta Ramadasu related to Madanna and Akkanna?
x: Bhakta Ramadasu was the nephew of Madanna and Akkanna.

s: In which year was Guru Tegh Bahadur executed by Aurangzeb at Chandni Chowk, Delhi?
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed at Chandni Chowk in Delhi in 1675 by order of Aurangzeb.

s: Which Sikh Guru built the Akal Takht?
x: Guru Hargobind, the sixth Guru, built the Akal Takht and was imprisoned at Gwalior.

s: The first matrimonial alliance with the Rajputs was established by Akbar with the house of :
x: The first matrimonial alliance with the Rajputs was established by Akbar with Kachhwaha Rajput. He went on a pilgrimage to the Mausoleum of Shaikh Muinuddin Chishti at Ajmer in 1562 A.D. His route laid through the Rajput state of Amber. Its ruler Raja Bihari Mal (Bharmal), with a view of safeguarding his position, offered his submission to Akbar at Sanganer and voluntarily proposed his daughter, Princess Harkhabai (Jodha) marriage with the young monarch. Akbar accepted the offer and on his return from Ajmer, married in 1562 AD. It was the first marriage of Akbar with any Rajput girl. Thus, Raja Bharmal was the first Rajput king who accepted Akbar’s supremacy of his accord. Salim (later Jahangir), heir to the throne was born of this wedlock on August 30, 1569 AD.

s: The Mughal Emperor who appointed the maximum number of Hindu officials was –
Which of the following pairs (battle during the Mughal and Maratha Period and its year) is correctly matched?
x: Battle of Haldighati was fought between Maharana Pratap and Akbar's forces led by Man Singh of Amber in 1576 A.D. Battle of Chausa was fought between Humayun and Shershah in June, 1539. Battle of Kannauj or Bilgram was fought between Humayun and Shershah in May, 1540. Battle of Kheda was fought between Shahu and Tarabai for the Maratha throne in 1707 A.D. Battle of Khajwa was fought between Mughal emperor Aurangzeb and Shah Suza in January, 1659.

s:
Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order:
1. Murder of Abul Fazl
2. Death of Sheikh Mubarak
3. Death of Faizi
4. Death of Daniyal
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
x: Sheikh Mubarak, who was the father of Abul Fazl and Faizi, passed away in 1593 CE. Faizi died in 1595 CE. The assassination of Abul Fazl occurred in 1602 CE on the orders of Prince Salim. Akbar's son Daniyal passed away in 1605 CE. Thus, the correct chronological order is 2, 3, 1, 4.

s:
Arrange the following events of Akbar’s regime in their chronological order :
1. Abolition of Jizya
2. Construction of Ibadat Khana
3. Signing of Mahzar
4. Foundation of Din-i-Ilahi
Select the correct answer from the codes given below :
x: Akbar abolished Jizya in 1564 A.D.. The construction of Ibadat Khana occurred in 1575 A.D. whose main purpose was to facilitate philosophical and theological discussions. The declaration of Mahzarnama was held in 1579 A.D. which was prepared by Shaikh Mubarak, the father of Abul Fazl. Akbar founded Din-i-Ilahi in 1582 A.D. for religious harmony.

s: Which of the following about Akbar's religious measures is NOT correct?
o: The Ibadat Khana was built in 1575.
The Mahzar preceded the construction of the Ibadat Khana.
x: The Mahzar (1579) came after the Ibadat Khana (1575); the order is jizya abolished 1564, Ibadat Khana 1575, Mahzar 1579, Din-i-Ilahi 1582.

s: Under Akbar's Karori experiment (1574), how much revenue was each circle meant to yield?
x: Each circle was to yield one crore dams, hence the name 'karori'.

s: What did the mansabdari and zabti-dahsala systems together give the Mughal state?
o: A salaried, transferable nobility and predictable cash revenue
A hereditary nobility and tribute from autonomous chiefs
Religious endowments in place of military service
Revenue in kind collected directly from every village
x: Mansabdari and zabti-dahsala together provided a salaried, transferable nobility and a predictable stream of cash revenue.

s: In which year was Akbar's Karori experiment introduced?
x: The Karori experiment was in 1574; the Dahsala followed in 1580.

s: Under the Karori experiment, what were the officers in charge of the revenue circles called?
x: Each circle yielding one crore dams was under an officer called a karori.

s: The first person to be given proper status of the Diwan by Akbar was -
x: Diwan is a word in Persian vocabulary and was adopted by Muslims during the period of Umar Caliph. They used that term for the treasury department. Muzaffar Khan Turbati was made Diwan (with Todar Mal as assistant) early in Akbar's reign. Todar Mal and Khwaja Shah Mansur later served in the finance ministry. The growth of the Diwan’s department began with the appointment of Muzaffar Khan Turbati. Diwan was a supreme official of financial affairs and revenues.

s: Upon whose earlier survey-based system did Todar Mal's revenue arrangements build?
x: Todar Mal had earlier served Sher Shah and built upon Sher Shah's survey-based system.

s: Of what was the improved jarib made, which avoided shrinking or stretching in land measurement?
o: Bamboo pieces joined with iron rings
x: The jarib was made of bamboo pieces joined with iron rings, which avoided the shrinkage or stretching of hemp rope.

s: Todar Mal held which office in the Mughal Empire?
x: Todar Mal served as the Diwan, or finance minister, of the empire and was also counted among the Navratnas.

s: Which of the following about the state share under Todar Mal's revenue arrangement is NOT correct?
o: It was one-third of the average produce.
It was normally paid in cash called dam.
Payment in kind was allowed in some areas.
It was paid in cash called jital.
x: The state share was paid in cash called dam, not jital, though payment in kind was allowed in some areas.

s: About how long was the Gaz-i-Ilahi, Akbar's unit of length?
x: The Gaz-i-Ilahi was about 82 cm.

s: Who was the first to be given the proper status of Diwan by Akbar, with Todar Mal as his assistant?
x: Akbar first gave the proper status of Diwan to Muzaffar Khan Turbati; Todar Mal and Khwaja Shah Mansur came later.

s: The "Dahsala" system developed by Raja Todar Mal was for
o: Collection of land revenue at standard rate which was valid for 10 years
Measurement of land once in 10 years for fixing area of assessment
Collection of revenue on the basis of average of produce and prices in the last 10 years
Sharing of crop between the farmer and the State for 10 years
x: Dahsala (1580) assessed revenue on the average produce and prices of the previous ten years (1571-80), converted into cash. It was not a fixed ten-year rate, a decennial survey or crop-sharing.

s: Which revenue system among the following is also known as the Bandobast System?
x: ‘Dahsala’ was a land revenue system during Akbar’s reign which was also known as Bandobast system.

s: Zabti system was introduced by –
x: Zabti System was introduced for land revenue in the reign of Akbar which was measurement based assessment; revenue circles (dasturs) with per-bigha cash rates; Ain-i-Dahsala (ten year average rate). It was based on schedules of Dasturul-Amal and Zabti Khasre for land survey and land revenue determination. Most of the area was based on this system. 33. In which measures Todarmal achieved fame ? (a) Military campaign (b) Land Revenue (c) Humor (d) Painting U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1992 Ans. (b) Todarmal achieved fame in the field of land revenue. Akbar introduced the Dahsala or Zabti system of land revenue collection in 1580 A.D. to consolidate Mughal empire. The founder of this system was Todarmal under Akbar. That’s why it is known as Todarmal settlement. Under this system, the average produce of different crops, as well as the average prices prevailing over the last ten years, was calculated. Onethird of the average produce was state Share (Maal), rest two-third share was left to the cultivators (Kharaj).

s: Todarmal was associated to –
x: Akbar appointed Raja Todarmal and Muzaffar Khan Turbati as finance minister for re-assessment of the land revenue system. He calculated the average produce of different crops as well as average price prevailing over the last ten years from 1571 to 1580 AD. One-third of that average was fixed as land revenue for state which was also called “Dahsala System”. Ain-i-Dahsala is known as Todarmal Bandobast.’

s: Which of the following systems were prevailing basis of land revenue collection in the Deccan during the reign of Akbar?
x: In J.N. Sarkar's book 'History of Aurangzeb', it has been mentioned on page number 190, that in North India during the reign of Akbar systematic method of land revenue collection was established by Dewan Todarmal, but this type of systematic method was not found in the Deccan. During this period the farmers of the Deccan used to pay land revenue to the state on per plough (number of plough) basis.

s: Which revenue system among the following was also known as the Bandobast system?
x: Dahsala (Ain-i-Dahsala) is the system called Bandobast, also known as Zabti or Bandobast and associated with Todar Mal. Nasaq and Kankut are different methods (past records and standing-crop estimate).

s: During the reign of Akbar, the role of an official called Amalguzar was
o: to be in-charge of law and order.
to make an assessment and collection of land revenue.
to be in-charge of imperial household.
x: The Amalguzar was the sarkar-level revenue collector, responsible for assessing and collecting land revenue and extending cultivation. Law and order was the faujdar's task, and the treasury was kept by the potdar.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Zabti — Crop-sharing between the state and peasant
Batai — Rough assessment based on past revenue records
Kankut — Yield estimated on the standing crop
Nasaq — Land measured and cash rates fixed per crop
x: Kankut involved estimating the yield on the standing crop. Zabti involved measurement and cash rates, Batai involved crop-sharing, and Nasaq relied on past revenue records.

s: In which region was the Nasaq method of revenue assessment mainly used under the Mughals?
x: Nasaq was used mainly in Bengal; Batai in Thatta, Kabul and Kashmir, Zabti in the core provinces, plough-based assessment in parts of the Deccan.

s: In which year was Akbar's Dahsala system introduced?
x: Dahsala, based on ten-year average produce and prices commuted into cash, came in 1580; 1574 was the Karori experiment.

s: The Dahsala was based on the average produce and prices of which years?
x: The Dahsala (1580) used the average of the last ten years, 1571-1580.

s: Where was Batai (Ghalla-bakhshi) mainly used under the Mughals?
x: Crop-sharing (batai) was used in Thatta, Kabul and Kashmir; Nasaq was mainly in Bengal and Zabti in the core provinces.

s: Under Akbar's Zabti system, what were the 'dasturs'?
o: Cash revenue rates per crop per bigha
Revenue circles yielding one crore dams
x: Under zabti, land was measured and dasturs fixed cash rates per crop per bigha.

s: In parts of the Deccan, on what basis was land revenue fixed under the plough method?
o: An estimate of the standing crop
x: In parts of the Deccan revenue was assessed by the number of ploughs.

s: Under Akbar's land classification, what was land left fallow for one or two years called?
x: Parauti lay fallow one or two years; Polaj was cultivated every year, Chachar fallow three or four years, Banjar five or more.

s: Under Akbar's land classification, what was land left uncultivated for five years or more called?
x: Banjar was fallow 5+ years; Parauti 1-2 and Chachar 3-4 years.

s: In Akbar's classification, what kind of land was Polaj?
x: Polaj land was cultivated every year.

s: In Mughal administrative vocabulary ‘Maal’ represents–
x: It was related to Land Revenue.

s: ‘Madad-i-Mash’ indicates in Mughal administration –
o: Revenue free land granted to learned persons
x: Sometimes, the Mughal administration issued grants as a Madad-i-Maash to pious or otherwise worthy recipients as charity. The spirit of composite culture and harmony expressed in revenue-free grants (Madad-i-Maash), which the nobles extended to the support of saints, maintenance of religious institutions, religious places and upkeep of Mashaikhs, etc.

s: In the Mughal administration ‘Madad- i-Mash’ indicates
o: revenue free land given to learned persons
x: Madad-i-maash was a revenue-free grant to scholars, holy men and the needy, so option 2 is correct. It was not a tax or a military pension.

s: What was Mughal crown land, whose revenue went straight to the imperial treasury, called?
x: Crown land was khalisa; suyurghal and madad-i-maash were charitable revenue-free grants.

s: What did a jagir represent under the Mughal system?
o: A direct cash payment from the khalisa treasury
The right to collect revenue in lieu of salary, without ownership
A permanent revenue-free grant to scholars
x: A jagir was an assignment of the right to collect revenue in lieu of salary; it did not confer ownership of the land.

s: What were Mughal revenue-free grants to scholars, holy men and the needy called?
x: Madad-i-maash (also suyurghal) was a charitable revenue-free grant; Khalisa was crown land.

s: What was the principal source of income of the Mughal state?
x: Maal, the land revenue, was the main income of the Mughal state.

s: What did the term 'Suyurghal' mean in the Mughal period?
x: Suyurghal, like madad-i-maash, was a revenue-free grant to scholars, holy men and the needy.

s:
Assertion (A) : During the time of Akbar, for every ten cavalrymen, the mansabdars had to maintain twenty horses.
Reason (R) : Horses had to be rested while on march and replacements were necessary in times of war.
o: Both (A) and (R) is true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
x: During the reign of Akbar, for every ten cavalrymen, the Mansabdars had to maintain twenty horses. The main reason for this custom was that it was essential to give rest to the horses during the long journey and it was needed to replace horses during the war. Thus, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) both are correct, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

s: Which feature distinguished Mughal mansabdars from the British ICS?
o: They were paid only fixed treasury salaries
x: Mansabdars held combined civil-military, non-hereditary ranks paid by jagir; the ICS was purely civil and salaried.

s: In which tradition did the Mughal mansabdari system have its origin?
x: Mansabdari was of Central Asian / Mongol military origin.

s: Under Akbar, to whom alone were mansabs above those of the nobles (5,000, later 7,000) given?
x: Noble ranks ran from 10 to 5,000 (later 7,000); higher ranks were only for royal princes.

s:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's mansabdari system:
1. Zat denoted personal rank and pay.
2. Sawar denoted the number of horsemen to be maintained.
3. Mansabs were hereditary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Zat was personal rank and Sawar the horsemen to be kept; mansabs were non-hereditary.

s: In which class was a mansabdar whose sawar rank equalled his zat rank placed?
x: By the sawar-zat ratio, sawar equal to zat made a mansabdar first class.

s: What was the range of mansab ranks for nobles under Akbar?
x: Nobles held mansabs from 10 to 5,000 (later 7,000); higher ranks went only to princes.

s: Which type of Mughal jagir was hereditary and not transferable?
x: Watan jagir, the zamindar's homeland, was hereditary and not transferable.

s: After how many years were Tankha jagirs, given in lieu of salary, normally transferred?
x: Tankha jagirs were transferable every 3-4 years, which prevented local power bases.

s: Which of the following pairs (Jagir type – feature) is correctly matched?
o: Mashrut – conditional, tied to specified duties
x: Mashrut was conditional; Watan was non-transferable, In'am carried no service obligation and Tankha was in lieu of salary.

s: Which Mughal central minister handled military matters such as dagh, chehra and promotions?
x: The Mir Bakhshi was the military head in charge of dagh, chehra and promotions.

s: What was the Mughal Sadr-us-sudur in charge of?
x: The Sadr-us-sudur dealt with religious affairs, charitable grants and the Shariat.

s: Which of the following about Mughal central ministers is NOT correct?
o: The Mir Saman was in charge of religious affairs.
The Wakil was the highest in rank.
The Wazir handled revenue, treasury and accounts.
x: The Mir Saman looked after the royal household and karkhanas; religious affairs were with the Sadr-us-sudur.

s: Which Mughal central minister looked after the royal household and the karkhanas?
x: The Mir Saman was in charge of the royal household and karkhanas.

s: In medieval Deccan, Deshmukh was a village official, wh responsible to-
o: Collect land revenue from the peasants and to deposit it in the State treasury
Maintain law and order in the village
x: In the medieval Deccan administrative system, the Deshmukh was a local official responsible for collecting land revenue from villages. The Deshmukh collected revenue from peasants and forwarded it to the state treasury, functioning as an intermediary between the state administration and rural society.

s:
Match the following revenue officials during the reign of Akbar with their duties:
List I
List II
a. Amalguzar
I. Kept records of the revenue payable by the villages
b. Karkuns
II. Revenue Collector in-charge of a District
c. Qanungo
III. Accountant
d. Bitikchi
IV. Prepared the seasonal crop statistics
x: The amalguzar was the revenue collector, the qanungo kept revenue records, and the bitikchi kept records on land and produce, with the karkun preparing crop statistics. The option a-II, b-IV, c-I, d-III matches this pattern.

s: Who was the head of a Mughal suba, served by a Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi?
x: The Subedar headed the suba; the Diwan, Bakhshi, Sadr and Qazi were the other suba officials.

s: Under the Qutb Shahis of Golconda, the state generally took what share of the produce?
x: Golconda generally took one-third of the produce, not one-half.

s: Which of the following pairs (Unit – Officials) is correctly matched?
x: The pargana had the shiqdar, amil and qanungo. The sarkar had the faujdar and amalguzar, the town the kotwal, and the village the muqaddam, patwari and chowkidar.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Faujdar — military and law-and-order duties at the sarkar level
Subahdar — governor responsible for law and order
Provincial Diwan — revenue administration and an independent check on the governor
Kotwal — maintenance of pargana land and revenue records
x: The Kotwal was responsible for law and order in the city. Maintenance of land and revenue records at the pargana level was the duty of the Qanungo.

s: Which Mughal official kept the land and revenue records of a pargana?
x: The qanungo kept pargana land and revenue records; the potdar was a treasurer.

s: What was the Potdar in Mughal revenue administration?
x: The potdar was the treasurer; the patwari was the village accountant and the amalguzar the sarkar revenue collector.

s: In 1580, Akbar's empire was divided into how many subas?
x: There were 12 subas in 1580.

s: Whose duty was law and order in a Mughal town?
x: The kotwal kept law and order in the city; the faujdar did so at sarkar level.

s: In Mughal revenue administration, what was the duty of the Bitikchi?
o: Collecting the revenue of the sarkar
Keeping records on land and produce
Maintaining law and order in towns
x: The bitikchi kept records on land and produce; the amalguzar collected revenue and the potdar was treasurer.

s: Who was the revenue collector of a Mughal sarkar, also charged with extending cultivation?
x: The amalguzar collected sarkar revenue and tried to extend cultivation.
